subject: Post-call: prioritization and evaluation playbook for POC
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Liyuan Zhao <liyuan@brightline-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-20 14:12 -07:00
Subject: Post-call: prioritization and evaluation playbook for POC

Hi Liyuan — thanks again for the call today, great context on the customer-service workflows and peak-season constraints. Below is a short recap and a proposal for the POC evaluation playbook so we can lock timelines. Please confirm or update by EOD Tuesday.

Quick recap of ask from Brightline:
- Ingest QA + order history (30 days sample) to evaluate intent routing and resolution rates
- Two priority outcomes: 1) accurate routing to human/automated path, 2) extraction of refund/return reason for SR automation
- Tight latency requirement for web chat: 95th pct < 250ms in our expected traffic mix

Proposed POC success criteria (draft):
- Routing accuracy: macro F1 >= 0.86 on held-out test set for prioritized intents
- Refund reason extraction: exact-match >= 78% on normalized labels (allowing for synonyms)
- Latency: 95th percentile generation latency < 250ms for 8k token window (production-like sampling)
- Stability: no more than 2% error rate on repeated inference during high-concurrency test

Proposed timeline (three weeks):
1) Week 0 (this week): access and sample ingestion, sign addendum for added use case
2) Week 1: baseline runs + evaluation harness; daily sync with Brightline CS owner
3) Week 2: iteration (prompting, quantization/profile), final evaluation and handoff

Immediate asks from our side:
- Confirm acceptance criteria above or list adjustments (especially F1 thresholds)
- Provide a 30-day order history sample (anonymized) or S3 access with read-only role
- Copy of procurement contact for a two-week SOW addendum

Ive attached a short outline (poc-addendum draft) and a sample ingest spec. If the refund-extraction use case is higher priority than routing, tell us and we can rebalance resources.

Thanks — I will follow up internally to align owners.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0132
From: Liyuan Zhao <liyuan@brightline-retail.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightline-retail.com
Date: 2026-08-20 15:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: prioritization and evaluation playbook for POC

Thanks Jonas — great summary. A couple of updates from our side after internal sync:
- Please add refund/reason extractor as a co-primary use case; this is the driver for automation savings in Q4.
- For routing accuracy we would like target F1 >= 0.89 (we have internal tolerance at 0.9 but can accept 0.89 for POC).
- For extraction, could we aim for 80% exact-match on normalized labels? 78 feels a touch low for our ops team.
- Security/compliance: can you send the SOC2 summary and any data-handling checklist we should share with Legal? procurement looped in for the SOW addendum.

We can provide an anonymized 30-day sample by Thursday; I will have procurement push the S3 details to you and Ben. Also cc's: rachel.kim@brightline-retail.com (owner of refunds) — she will be in the eval loop.

If you can adjust the timeline to give our ops team one extra week for verification, that would be ideal (so move final evaluation to Week 3).

Appreciate it — Liyuan

Liyuan Zhao
Head of ML Platforms | Brightline Retail
liyuan@brightline-retail.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-20 15:35 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: prioritization and evaluation playbook for POC

Forwarding Liyuan's reply — key asks: bump routing F1 to 0.89, extraction target to 80%, add refund extractor as co-primary, one-week timeline extension, procurement will provide S3 details.

Can you both confirm owners and whether the latency target stays feasible if we shift the iteration window? Also Ben, given the extra use case, do we need a bigger sample or different eval harness?

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-20 17:08 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: prioritization and evaluation playbook for POC

Thanks — I can take the technical lead for the extended POC. Quick notes:
- Owner assignments: Ben = ingest + baseline + latency profiling; Marissa = success criteria owner + evaluation tracker + customer syncs
- Data needs: anonymized 30-day sample is fine but please include a separate small file of labeled refund cases (~500 rows) so we can bootstrap extractor fine-tuning and evaluate exact-match quickly
- Eval plan adjustments:
  * Keep routing F1 target at 0.89 per request
  * Extraction: aim for 80% exact-match; we'll also report token-level F1 for partial credit
  * Latency: I will run a production-like concurrency test and report 95th pct. If we enable quantized model variant for inference we should hit 95th < 250ms; I will validate during Week 2.
- Timeline: Ben confirms we need an extra week for iteration; propose overall 4-week cadence (ingest+baseline = 1 week, tuning = 2 weeks, final eval = 1 week)

Attachments I will drop to the shared drive: ingest spec and baseline script outline. Ben

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Liyuan Zhao <liyuan@brightline-retail.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, procurement@brightline-retail.com
Date: 2026-08-21 09:42 -07:00
Subject: POC addendum & confirmed owners — next steps

Hi all — looping in the agreed updates and a clear set of next steps so Brightline can circulate internally. I have attached a one-page addendum and the evaluation spreadsheet template. Summary:
- Confirmed success criteria: routing F1 >= 0.89; extraction exact-match >= 80%; latency 95th < 250ms
- Owners: Jonas = commercial lead; Ben = technical lead; Marissa = success criteria & acceptance tracker (final decisions rest with Brightline ops)
- Data deliverables due: anonymized 30-day sample + labeled refund file (~500 rows) by 2026-08-26
- Infra and access: read-only S3 credentials (or presigned objects) to ben@redwood.com; if Legal needs SOC2 we included SOC2-summary-Redwood.pdf in attachments
- Timeline: kick-off ingest on 2026-08-27; baseline complete by 2026-09-03; tuning complete by 2026-09-17; final evaluation and review week of 2026-09-20
- Deliverables at close: eval report, export of confusion matrices, model variant recommendation, and handoff package for production rollout

Next steps for Brightline: procurement to send S3 details and countersign the addendum. Jonas — I'll create the shared Drive folder and upload the evaluation tracker now: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/brightline-poc-plan

I'll also open a short DocuSign for the addendum (link in related links). If that timeline looks good Liyuan, I'll mark owners in the tracker and schedule the 30-min kickoff for 2026-08-27 10:00am PT.

Thanks — Marissa
